newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
RECORD NUMBER OF CHALLENGERS FOR 2000 AMERICA'S CUP
The deadline for challengers for the 2000 America's Cup in Auckland, New Zealand passed this week with a late flurry of entries to post a record 18 boats from 10 nations.
"The Auld Mug is alive and well," said JOHN HEISE, commodore of the defending club the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron.
The previous record was 13 syndicates from six nations fronting up for the first ever Down Under defence of the America's Cup at Fremantle in 1987.

DENNIS CONNER will be back again, with CHRIS DICKSON as an ally instead of an enemy. PETER GILMOUR will be at the helm, albeit for the Japanese, PAUL CAYARD and JOHN KOLIUS will be helming two of the five U.S. boats, and SYD FISCHER will make history with his fifth challenge.
While defender Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron and Team New Zealand will almost certainly have world match racing champion RUSSELL COUTTS back at the helm.
With such a line-up it promises to be the greatest America's Cup regatta since we defended the Auld Mug back in 1986-87 and will run from October 1999 to March 2000.

While 70-year-old FISCHER, who this week challenged through the Cruising Yacht of Australia, will be Australia's only representative, that may well be the vital incentive to mount his bestever of attempts to win the Cup.
More importantly, it should direct vital commercial sponsorship to his campaign, along with design support from IAIN MURRAY, our most experienced Cup designer.

MURRAY and his design company, Iain Murray Associates, were left out in the cold by the surprise decision of Sydney businessman DENIS O'NEIL not to go ahead with a challenge through the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron. O'NEIL was to have been chairman of the syndicate, MURRAY the executive director.

One of the reasons for not going ahead was the inability of the O'NEIL/MURRAY syndicate to purchase with full legal title the assets of the 1995 OneAustralia challenge which included one International America's Cup Class yacht, its masts and sails, shorebase equipment and vital computer data.

While FISCHER also has his 1995 challenger, Sydney 95, plus a range of other designs, let's hope that he can get together with MURRAY in working towards a strong challenge in 2000. It would be a fine gesture for those involved in the oneAustralia litigation to make the boat and equipment available to FISCHER and the Cruising Yacht Club for America's Cup 2000.

The challenge of DENNIS CONNER, the only yachtsman to twice lose the America's Cup (1983 and 1995), is not through the San Diego Yacht Club for whom he regained the Cup at Fremantle in 1987. Instead, he is challenging through the Cortez Yachting Association, the group which organises the most popular yacht racing in San Diego, the Wednesday afternoon "Beer Can Race."
SYDNEY-BUILT W60 HEADING FOR BRITAIN

The chances of an Australian yacht contesting the 1997-98 Whitbread round-the-world race look virtually nil, but at least we will have an Australian-built Whitbread 60 in the 33,000 nautical mile circumnavigation.

Silk Cut, built by Sydney boatbuilder JOHN McCONAGHY, will be airlifted to Britain over the weekend aboard an Antanov 124/100, a giant Russian airfreighter, where it is due at Stansted airport on Tuesday.
Silk Cut will be skippered in the Whitbread by LAWRIE SMITH, joining a fleet of between nine and a dozen W60s from the United States, Britain, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden and Holland.
PITTWATER TO NOUMEA RACE IN SEPTEMBER

Sydney's Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club will join with Brisbane's Queensland Cruising Yacht Club and New Caledonia's Cercel Nautique Caledonien in maintaining the Australia to Noumea international ocean race, with fleets starting from Pittwater on September 12 and from Moreton Bay two days later.

The first race to Noumea was back in 1953 and have been conducted by the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia. The popular race across the South Pacific lost some of its momentum and appeal during the French nuclear testing in the Pacific.
The CYCA elected not to run the event this year and the option was taken up by the QCYC, but with added Sydney interest, the club approached the RPAYC to run a Sydney division.

Already six Alfreds yacht owners have put up their hands as potential competitors, including Commodore BRUCE STAPLES with his multiple race winner, Canon Copiers, and past Commodore RICHARD HUDSON with former Sydney-Hobart winner Indian Pacific.

Record for the 1,050 nautical mile voyage from Sydney is five days 21 hours and 35 minutes set by GEORGE SNOW in his former maxi Brindabella, now Infinity III. It would be great to see the former and present Brindabellas heading for Noumea.
Snow enjoys long ocean passage races to warmer climes and tomorrow he will sail his cruiser/racer Infinity II in the second annual race from Brisbane to Gizo in the Solomon Islands.
Organised by the Royal Queensland Yacht Squadron, the race to Gizo has attracted a fleet of 22 starters, including two New Zealand yachts.
VICTORIAN YACHTSMAN'S GREAT SEASON
The Royal Yacht Club of Victoria has won back the prestigious Association Cup from across-the-bay rivals Sandringham Yacht Club, climaxing a great season for the Williamstown club.
The Association Cup, a teams event, marked the end of the summer sailing season in Melbourne and the winning club is regarded as the premier keelboat club on Port Phillip.

The Royals team was Chutzpah, skippered by past Commodore and prominent Collins street orthodontist BRUCE TAYLOR, the 1995 Sydney-Hobart winner Terra Firma, owned by young computer company directors DEAN WILSON and SCOTT CARLILE, Western Morning, skippered by JUSTIN BRENNAN, and First Light sailed by RON LAYTON.

The win by the Royals team capped a successful season for TAYLOR in his ROBERT HICK designed Chutzpah. He also won both the IMS and VYC divisions of the six race Becks series on the bay and took out the Ocean Racing Club of Victoria's summer ocean racing pointsocore.
But one trophy still eludes TAYLOR - the Sydney-Hobart.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
